segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good morning, and welcome to the museum – one with a remarkable range of exhibits, which I’m sure you’ll enjoy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My name’s Greg, and I’ll tell you about the various collections as we go round.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But before we go, let me just give you a taste of what we have here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, for one thing, we have a fine collection of twentieth and twenty-first century paintings, many by very well-known artists.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I’m sure you’ll recognise several of the paintings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is the gallery that attracts the largest number of visitors, so it’s best to go in early in the day, before the crowds arrive.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The there are the nineteenth-century paintings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The museum was opened in the middle of that century, and several of the artists each donated one work – to get the museum started, as it were.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So they’re of special interest to us – we feel closer to them than to other works.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The sculpture gallery has a number of fine exhibits, but I’m afraid it’s currently closed for refurbishment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You’ll need to come back next year to see it properly, but a number of the sculptures have been moved to other parts of the museum. ‘Around the world’ is a temporary exhibition – you’ve probably seen something about it on TV or in the newspapers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s created a great deal of interest, because it presents objects from every continent and many countries, and provides information about their social context – why they were made, who for, and so on.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then there’s the collection of coins.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is what you might call a focused, specialist collection, because all the coins come from this country, and were produced between two thousand and a thousand years ago.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And many of them were discovered by ordinary people digging their gardens and donated to the museum! All our porcelain and glass we left to the museum by its founder, when he died in 1878.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And in the terms of his will, we’re not allowed to add anything to that collection: he believed it was perfect in itself, and we don’t see any reason to disagree! ——————– OK, that was something about the collections, and now here’s some more practical information, in case you need it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most of the museum facilities are downstairs, in the basement, so you go down the stairs here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When you reach the bottom of the stairs, you’ll find yourself in a sitting area, with comfortable chairs and sofas where you can have a rest before continuing your exploration of the museum.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We have a very good restaurant, which serves excellent food all day, in a relaxing atmosphere.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: To reach it, when you get to the bottom of the stairs, go straight ahead to the far side of the sitting area, then turn right into the corridor.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You’ll see the door on the restaurant facing you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you just want a snack, or if you’d like to eat somewhere with facilities for children, we also have a café.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When you reach the bottom of the stairs, you’ll need to go straight ahead, turn right into the corridor, and the café is immediately on the right. And talking about children, there are baby-changing facilities downstairs: cross the sitting area, continue straight ahead along the corridor on the left and you and your body will find the facilities on the left-hand side. The cloakroom where you should leave coats, umbrella and any large bags, is on the left hand side of the sitting area.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s through the last door before you come to the corridor. There are toilets on every floor, but in the basement they’re the first rooms on the left when you get down there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK, now if you’ve got anything to leave in the cloakroom, please do that now, and then we’ll start our tour.
